newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian federal election voting breakdown.
newsitem.headline: Canadian federal election voting breakdown.

text.p: Following are unofficial final results from the June 2, 1997 Canadian federal election, in number of parliamentary seats won, gain/loss from 1993, and popular vote. Liberals: 155 seats (-22), 38 pct of vote.
Bloc Quebecois: 44 seats (-10), 11 pct of vote. Conservatives: 20 seats (+18), 19 pct of vote. New Democrats: 21 seats (+12), 11 pct of vote. Other: 1 seat (0), 2 pct of vote.
A total of 301 seats were up for grabs in 1997, compared to 295 in 1993.

Voter turnout was lower than previous elections, with 67 percent of Canada's 13 million eligible voters casting ballots, down from 69.9 per cent in 1993. An average of 75 percent of Canadians have exercised their franchise over the last dozen federal elections.
